messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: GPU pool eu-west-1-gpu-1 at 100% utilization and autoscaler failing to provision nodes. Pager: alex (oncall).

alex: I'm on it. Paging @priya + @megan. What's the symptom set?

priya: Queue growth on inference-queue — ~5000 pending, p50 latency -> 2.2s, p95 -> 12s. Autoscaler logs show `scaleUp: rejected by quota` and provider returning 429s.

megan: Confirming provider 429s for createNode calls, one node stuck in provisioning. Checking cloud console and quota.

jonas: Runtime: lots of KV cache cold misses and slow shard attach times. Warmup spikes causing long start-up token costs. Fallbacks aren't absorbing traffic because routing still points to preferred variant.

alex: Can we route to a smaller quantized model temporarily (reduce compute per request)?

priya: We have redwood-v2-q4 as a fallback. If we can shift routing that's fastest. Also need to consider backing off client RPS to avoid control-plane amplification.

megan: Cloud shows insufficient capacity for g5s. Starting manual spin of alternative instance type g4dn in eu-west-1.

deploy-bot: Runbook step: to scale fallback pool run `infractl scale --pool=eu-gpu-fallback --replicas=8`.

alex: Kicking that now. Also dropping prefix cache TTL to reduce compute churn.

alex: `infractl scale --pool=eu-gpu-fallback --replicas=8` -> accepted, creating nodes. Applying routing change to fallbacks.

sarah: Support: customers are reporting 429s and slow responses. We'll prepare a status update once we have mitigation.

priya: Autoscaler log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:44Z autoscaler: requestScaleUp 12 -> attempt
2026-03-15T03:12:45Z provider: 429 RateLimitExceeded createNode
2026-03-15T03:13:01Z autoscaler: backoff increased to 30s
```

jonas: I'll flip routing to q4 for high-traffic endpoints. Command: `routerctl set-route /generate model=redwood-v2-q4 weight=70`

alex: Let's move fully — set weight to 100 for /generate-prod-temp so we see clear effect.

jonas: Setting to 100 for /generate-prod-temp now.

incident-bot: STATUS: fallback pool scale request accepted and routing change applied.

megan: Fallback g4dn nodes are starting, some in Ready. Provisioning of g4 still staggered — provider is throttling a bit. One node stuck in provisioning loop but others coming up.

priya: Queue length dropping: 5000 -> 980 -> 450 within ~6 minutes. p95 latency improving: 12s -> 3.4s.

sarah: Drafting status update: 'Experiencing elevated latency and 429s in eu-west-1 for inference. We have shifted traffic to alternate instance types and quantized models. Mitigation in progress, no data loss.' Will post in 10m unless told otherwise.

alex: Include endpoints (/generate, /chat) and advise degraded performance UX.

sarah: Will include.

megan: Note: provider quota for g5 hit. We should file quota increase request and consider reserved capacity for peak windows.

priya: Agreed. Action items: request quota increase, add 429 jitter/retry in autoscaler, and multi-instance-type fallback.

alex: Adding a temporary protective router rate-limit: `rate-limit --route /generate --rps 80`.

jonas: Enabling aggressive batching on q4 to reduce token cost per request.

deploy-bot: Observed autoscaler backoff behavior; recommend reducing scale-up step size for noisy windows (12->4). Runbook PR: https://repo/infra/runbooks/scale-tuning (suggested).

alex: Opening tickets for runbook updates and autoscaler tuning.

sarah: Customers asking for ETA.

alex: ETA: expecting stabilization within ~25 minutes from start of mitigation. Will update.

megan: All fallback nodes now Ready and registered. g4 provisioning settled; autoscaler attempted g5 again but received 429. g4 path succeeded.

priya: Queue at ~80 pending now. p95 latency ~1.1s. Behavior looks mitigated. Marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: MITIGATION: traffic routed to fallback model + fallback pool. Pager cleared?

alex: Clearing pager. Keeping thread open for postmortem and action items.

sarah: Customer impact summary: ~12 customers experienced degraded performance for ~22 minutes; 3 customers saw transient 429s on heavy write workloads. No data lost, retries handled.

megan: Preliminary root cause: provider capacity exhaustion for preferred instance type (g5) combined with autoscaler not falling back gracefully to alternate instance types because of rate limits and scale step size. Runtime cold-start behavior amplified queue growth.

priya: Postmortem action items:
- (A1) Autoscaler: implement multi-instance-type fallback and 429 backoff jitter. Owner: priya. Due: 2 weeks.
- (A2) Infra: reserve burst capacity for eu-west-1 (monthly commit) and file quota increase. Owner: megan. Due: 1 month.
- (A3) Runtime: improve shard warmup and faster readiness signals for attaching nodes. Owner: jonas. Due: 3 weeks.
- (A4) Runbooks: add explicit manual switch to quantized fallback model and routing commands. Owner: alex. Due: 1 week.
- (A5) Support: prepare customer outreach template and list affected customers. Owner: sarah. Due: 48 hours.

alex: I'll submit the runbook PR and schedule a post-incident review for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

sarah: I'll compile the customer list and draft outreach.

jonas: Adding telemetry alert for KV warmup misses and a regression monitor for cold-start latency.

megan: Opening provider quota ticket and asking for capacity guarantee for expected peak windows.

priya: Also propose adding a polite circuit breaker at router level for long-tail requests to avoid pile-up when backend capacity is degraded.

alex: Thanks team. Marking thread for follow-up and assigning owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: severity P2, duration 00:22:43. Thread archived for postmortem.
